# Flux

Plugin ID `flux`. Flux sources, kustomizations and Helm releases.

The GitOps page lists every Flux source, Kustomization and HelmRelease with its readiness, its
revision and, for sources, its signature verification. A failing or suspended object, and a
source that must be verified and is not, become attention items on the Overview. The plugin
reads the cluster through the kubernetes plugin, and is `unavailable` on a cluster that serves
none of the Flux kinds.

## What it shows

### Pages

| Page | Path |
|---|---|
| GitOps (Flux) | `/gitops` |

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Overview, KPI row (`overview.kpis`) | GitOps: ready objects and source verification | `gitops` |

### Contributions

It contributes attention items and KPIs.

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `flux.objects` | `FluxData` | Flux sources, kustomizations and Helm releases. |

## Dependencies

A change to a plugin's settings restarts it and the plugins that require or use it.

- **Requires** [Kubernetes](kubernetes.md): while it does not run or is `unavailable`, this plugin is `blocked` and its pages are hidden.

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.flux` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginsflux), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.flux.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.flux.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.flux.suspendReasonAnnotation` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_SUSPEND_REASON_ANNOTATION` | string | - | no | no | Flux object annotation whose value is shown as the reason the object is suspended. Empty hides the reason. |
| `plugins.flux.verify.requireWhenSpecVerify` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_VERIFY_REQUIRE_WHEN_SPEC_VERIFY` | boolean | `true` | no | no | A GitRepository or OCIRepository that has spec.verify must report SourceVerified=True: without it the source is critical on the overview, in the verified tile and on the GitOps page. false puts only the sources listed in sources in scope, for the attention items, the tile and the page alike. The default is true. |
| `plugins.flux.verify.sources` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_VERIFY_SOURCES` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | Sources that must be signed and verified, as [{kind, namespace, name}] with kind GitRepository or OCIRepository. Each is critical on the overview when it lacks spec.verify or SourceVerified=True, or when it does not exist, and each is listed on the GitOps page. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.flux.actions.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ACTIONS_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | Offer the plugin's actions. Off by default: without it the actions are not mounted and the web UI does not show their buttons. |
| `plugins.flux.actions.denyNamespaces` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ACTIONS_DENY_NAMESPACES` | list of strings (JSON) | - | no | no | Namespaces the plugin's actions refuse, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.flux.actions.agents` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ACTIONS_AGENTS` | string | `approve` | no | no | What an AI agent's call of one of the plugin's action tools (MCP, a token with the mcp audience) does: deny hides the tools and refuses them, approve creates an approval request a person approves or denies in dash, allow runs the action at once. A target that needs its name typed (a protected namespace) always waits for a person's approval, even with allow. API tokens and signed-in people are never affected. The default is approve; applies live. |

- `plugins.flux.suspendReasonAnnotation`: the reason shows in the suspended warning's detail and
  on the GitOps page; empty shows "suspended" alone.
- The check that a `plugins.flux.verify.sources` entry exists is skipped while the list of its
  kind cannot be read, so a refused list never raises a false critical. An entry with an unknown
  field, another kind, no namespace or name, or a duplicate is refused when the configuration
  loads. In the environment:
  `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_VERIFY_SOURCES='[{"kind":"GitRepository","namespace":"gitops","name":"fleet"}]'`.

## Actions

### `reconcile`: Reconcile

`POST /api/v1/plugins/flux/actions/reconcile`, for administrators. Idempotent: repeating it with the same input is safe. Confirmation: none.

Input, a JSON object: `kind` (string, required, one of `Kustomization`, `HelmRelease`, `GitRepository`, `OCIRepository`, `HelmRepository`); `namespace` (string, required); `name` (string, required).

### Limits

- **Off by default.** The actions are mounted only while `plugins.flux.actions.enabled` is `true` (`DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ACTIONS_ENABLED`); until then their routes answer 404 and the web UI shows no button for them. A change restarts the plugin.
- **Administrators only.** A viewer gets 403 `forbidden`.
- **Rate limit.** One user may start 10 actions a minute, across every plugin's actions; more answer 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.
- **Strict input.** The body is JSON with only the fields above; a missing required field or a value outside its list answers 400 `invalid_input`.
- **Denied namespaces.** `plugins.flux.actions.denyNamespaces` (`DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ACTIONS_DENY_NAMESPACES`) lists namespaces where the actions answer 403, whatever the role.
- **Audited.** Each run is written to the audit log before it runs and again with its outcome; when that record cannot be written the action is refused (503 `audit_unavailable`). The 403 and 429 refusals above are recorded as denials, at most one per user (or, before sign-in, per peer) and reason a minute; a 404 or a 400 `invalid_input` is not.
- **Guardrail.** On Kubernetes, the Helm chart's admission policy holds dash's ServiceAccount to exactly the write these actions make, whatever RBAC grants: see [the guardrail](../deploy/kubernetes.md#the-guardrail).

- `reconcile` sets the `reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt` annotation of a source, Kustomization
  or HelmRelease, which asks Flux to reconcile it now. Until the actions are on, the GitOps page
  shows no Reconcile button. `kind` is one of the five Flux kinds; `namespace` and `name` are DNS
  names.

## Kubernetes RBAC

dash reads the cluster with its ServiceAccount. The Helm chart grants each group of rules below while the value named is set ([RBAC modes](../deploy/kubernetes.md#rbac-modes)); with `rbac.create: false`, grant them yourself.

**To read the Flux objects** (chart: `rbac.read`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [kustomizations]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [helmreleases]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [source.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [gitrepositories, ocirepositories, helmrepositories]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
```

**With `plugins.flux.actions.enabled` (the reconcile action)** (chart: `rbac.actions.fluxReconcile`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [kustomizations]
    verbs: [patch]
  - apiGroups: [helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [helmreleases]
    verbs: [patch]
  - apiGroups: [source.toolkit.fluxcd.io]
    resources: [gitrepositories, ocirepositories, helmrepositories]
    verbs: [patch]
```

The reconcile write goes through the kubernetes plugin's client.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing. Its actions are mounted and change nothing outside dash.

The reconcile action answers 202 and changes nothing.
